newsitem.title: USA: Convicted murder put to death in Arizona.
newsitem.headline: Convicted murder put to death in Arizona.

text.p: Convicted killer Randy Greenawalt, whose 1978 rampage of murder sent terror throughout Arizona, died by lethal injection early Thursday, prison officials said.
Officials said that Greenawalt, who killed four people following a prison break, was put to death at 12:07 a.m. at the state prison complex after receiving the fatal dose while strapped to a gurney.
The death dose -- a mixture of sodium pentothal, pancuronium bromide and potassium chloride -- killed the 47-year-old in three minutes, officials said.
Witnesses attending the execution reported that he told his sister he loved her before he died.

Greenawalt, who had declined all interview requests, spent the last 18 years on death row for what is generally regarded as one of the most notorious and bloodiest crime sprees in modern-day Arizona history.
He is the seventh person to be put to death since 1992, when Arizona resumed capital punishment after a 29-year absence. The last execution was in August.

Greenawalt was sentenced to death in March 1979, but various appeals delayed the sentence from being carried on several occasions. This time, his last-minute appeals were turned down by state and federal courts.
His last meal consisted of cheeseburgers, french fries, coffee and milk.

Greenawalt, who was serving a life sentence for a 1974 murder of a truck driver, earned his reputation as one of the state's best-known criminals when he broke out of prison with inmate Gary Tison July 30, 1978. Their flight was aided by guns smuggled in by Tison's three sons.
Together with the sons, the gang went on a 12-day crime spree of killing and stealing as they hopscotched through parts of three western states.

The night after the breakout, the killing started after they had a flat tire. The group flagged down a family near Quartzsite, Ariz., kidnapped them and drove them to a secluded spot before killing them with shotguns.

Killed were Marine Sgt. John Lyons, 24; his wife Donnelda, 23; and their 22-month-old son Christopher. Also shot to death was Theresa Tyson, 15, of Las Vegas, whose body was found a quarter of a mile away.
The rampage continued as the gang drove north in the family's car and other stolen vehicles.

They killed two Texas newlyweds in southwestern Colorado and stole their van. Margene and James Judge were bound and shot in the head. Greenawalt and the Tisons were never charged with these killings.

The end came in the early morning hours of Aug. 11, 1978, when local sheriff's deputies nabbed Greenawalt and Raymond and Ricky Tison after a bloody, 10-minute gun battle at a roadblock. Donald Tison was killed and Gary Tison fled to the desert, where he apparently died of exposure.

All three received death sentences in 1979, but Greenawalt's penalty was the only one that stuck. Ricky and Raymond Tison had there sentences changed to life in prison by a state Supreme Court in 1992.
